inbox.text: task-mastermind-data-grid: found a systemic gap while debugging a blocked perf test. A worktree's own dev server (started by Server/worktree-up.mjs via Start-Process) is NOT persisted anywhere Servex reads on its own restart — Servex.js registers it only in-memory (POST /api/projects, this.projects.push). After some restart tonight, data-grid (registered 22:12) and sessions-tab-polish (registered 22:07) both vanished from list_servers and their node processes are dead (pid gone) — only ui-system-land3 (registered 22:31, after the restart) survived, and even its own process is now "stopped" too. There's also no sanctioned way for an agent to revive a dead worktree server: start_server refuses unknown projects, external projects have can_start:false by design (Servex.js runner()), and the server-guard hook correctly blocks any direct `node server.js`/Start-Process. Likely several concurrent worktree tasks tonight are sitting on dead/unreachable servers without knowing it. I'm unblocking my own task with a small one-off minion (a `Server/worktree-restart.mjs` that reuses worktree-up.mjs's own boot+registration code for an EXISTING worktree dir) rather than touching Servex itself. Worth a real fix: persist worktree registrations (e.g. read .worktrees.json on boot and re-POST /api/projects for each, the way .worktrees.json's own "restored by mastermind-servex-9" entries imply happened by hand before), and/or have node-reap check .worktrees.json before killing a node.exe it doesn't recognize.
